Nmap Scripting Engine
The Nmap Scripting Engine (NSE) contains a set of additional functionalities
(like brute force, DNS enumeration, HTTP enumeration, etc.) that make Nmap
work like a boss. The Nmap team categorized all these functionalities into
different groups, shown here:
I
I Auth
I
I Broadcast
I
I Default
I
I Discovery
I
I DOS
I
I Exploit
I
I External
I
I Fuzzer
I
I Intrusive
(continued)

A common example is HTTP enumeration, an NSE script exists for this purpose.
To get the job done, we need to specify the port number that we’re targeting
first, and also, we will add the version scan (which is optional, but I recommend
it) to get juicier information:

amqp-info.nse                         http-mcmp.nse
oracle-sid-brute.nse
[...]
A common example is HTTP enumeration, an NSE script exists for this purpose.
To get the job done, we need to specify the port number that we’re targeting
first, and also, we will add the version scan (which is optional, but I recommend
it) to get juicier information:
$nmap -p [port number] -sV –script [NSE script name] [IP address / range]
root@kali:~# nmap -sV -p 80 --script http-enum 10.0.0.1
